key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion promote dense Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater porosity reduces long-term corrosion resistance and higher humidity lowers friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters to minimize coating defects can improve protection of Q235 steel, while service humidity should inform wear-performance assessment.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values, humidity ranges, or test durations, limiting quantitative comparison and service-life prediction.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
